clue.text: Stupid pot belly's back

parts.note: pot and dope are both slang for cannabis

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, so only the closing letter is kept

parts.note: last letter of belly

explanation.surface: An insult aimed at someone with a paunch, suggesting their pot belly says something about their brains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pot belly' reads as one phrase, but pot is cannabis and belly only lends its back letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Dopey is an informal adjective for slow-witted or foolish, a straight synonym.

clue.text: New doors mark development sites

indicators.note: something new is made afresh, so the letters are formed into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A builder marks out new doors on a property development site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Development' suggests housing estates, but here it is the developing of photographic film.
explanation.definitionFit: Photographers process film in unlit rooms, so these are where pictures get developed.

clue.text: Quiet avenue son covers in flags?

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
standard abbreviation for avenue
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A quiet street where a son decorates the houses with bunting and flags.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark warns that flags are not banners but flagstones, the flat slabs used for paths.
explanation.definitionFit: To pave is to lay a surface of stones or slabs, and flagstones are such paving.

clue.text: Unknown relation scratching head, shouting

indicators.note: to scratch out is to erase, so the opening letter is struck off

parts.note: x, y and z are the algebraic unknowns
a relation is a telling or narration of a story

explanation.surface: Someone puzzled by an unfamiliar relative, scratching their head, while voices are raised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relation' suggests a family member, but here it means an account, as in relating a tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Yelling is crying out loudly, a direct synonym of the participle used.

clue.text: Vital the writer's left with a set of books

parts.note: the writer is the setter, me, and 'the writer is' becomes I'M
port is the left side of a ship
taken as written
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: An author insists it is essential they have departed carrying a box set of novels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like departed, but it is the nautical side; NT is a common crossword abbreviation for the New Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something of great significance or essential value, plain synonyms.

clue.text: One grows flowers

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
to grow is to rise or increase

explanation.surface: A gardener who raises blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads as 'a person who cultivates flowers', but the word one is just the numeral and grows is a verb meaning goes up.
explanation.definitionFit: The iris is a garden plant with showy blooms, so the plural names several of them.

clue.text: Badly paining a composer

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters end up in a garbled order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A wince at music so poorly played it hurts the composer.
explanation.walkthrough: Niccolò Paganini was an Italian violin virtuoso and composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Paganini wrote violin works including the famous 24 Caprices, so he is a classical composer.

clue.text: Part of dinner is Ottoman dish

indicators.note: a part of something sits within it, so the letters lie inside the phrase that follows

parts.note: spans the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: One course at a meal is a Turkish speciality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ottoman dish' suggests Turkish food, but the dish is Italian and the letters run across the word break.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is a cooked rice preparation served as a course, so it is a dish.

clue.text: Perhaps gazelles asleep, not jumping around

indicators.note: letters that jump around leap out of place and settle into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Gazelles at rest, for once not leaping about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' signals that gazelles are one example of the wider group.
explanation.definitionFit: Gazelles are one kind of African antelope, so the definition gives an example of the class.

clue.text: Weary and tense, anger beginning to dissipate

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
ire is anger

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that is taken

parts.note: first letter of dissipate

explanation.surface: Someone exhausted and on edge, whose temper is only starting to fade.
explanation.walkthrough: Tense looks like an adjective about stress, but it is the grammar term, abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: Weary and tired are close synonyms for being worn out and lacking energy.

clue.text: Horrible idiot boyfriend returned grand

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a nit is a fool
a lover is a boyfriend
G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: A dreadful, foolish boyfriend came back, apparently thinking himself magnificent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grand' reads as splendid, but it is slang for a thousand pounds, abbreviated G.
explanation.definitionFit: Revolting means disgusting or repellent, a straightforward synonym of horrible.

clue.text: Celebrity holding India's instrument

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a star is a celebrity
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A famous musician clutching an Indian instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, the sitar is an Indian instrument, so India appears in both wordplay and theme.
explanation.definitionFit: The sitar is a long-necked plucked lute from South Asia, so it is a musical instrument.

clue.text: Break in ceremony limiting telepathy?

indicators.note: a limit forms the boundary around something, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: a rite is a ceremony
ESP, extrasensory perception, covers telepathy

explanation.surface: A pause in a ritual that restricts mind-reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break in' looks like a phrase about intrusion, but break alone is the definition and in is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A respite is a short rest or relief from something, so it is a pause.

clue.text: Annoyed, Newton calmed down without having succeeded

parts.note: N is the symbol for the newton, the unit of force

indicators.note: to be without something is to lack it, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: settled means calmed down
s is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees

explanation.surface: Isaac Newton, irritated, cooled off after his efforts failed.
explanation.walkthrough: Newton looks like the scientist, but it is the unit of force with symbol N.
explanation.definitionFit: To be nettled is to be irritated or provoked, as if stung by the plant.

clue.text: Heartless fury in power cut

indicators.note: without a heart means missing its centre, so the middle letter is removed

parts.note: outrage is fury

explanation.surface: A cruel rage felt when the electricity goes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fury in power' suggests rage at someone in office, but power cut is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An outage is a period when a supply such as electricity is interrupted.

clue.text: Wrestling take-down grips old martial art

indicators.note: to grip is to hold, so one piece holds another
wrestling twists and contorts, so these letters are twisted into new places

parts.note: taken as written
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A wrestling move that brings an opponent down belongs to an ancient fighting discipline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrestling' and 'take-down' read as a single sporting scene, but wrestling is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Tae kwon do is a Korean combat sport of kicks and punches, a martial art.

clue.text: Relative bored by academic publisher's release

indicators.note: something bored is drilled through, so another piece sits inside it

parts.note: an uncle is a relative
OUP is Oxford University Press

explanation.surface: A family member finds a university press's new book tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bored' suggests tedium, but it means drilled into; 'publisher's' hides 'publisher is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To uncouple is to disconnect or set free, as with railway carriages, so it means let go.

clue.text: They test former American pit workers

parts.note: ex means former
A is an abbreviation for American
miners work in a pit

explanation.surface: Inspectors who check on retired coal miners from the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They test' is a whole definition by description: the plural pronoun stands for the people who set tests.
explanation.definitionFit: Examiners are those who set and mark exams or inspect things, so they test.

clue.text: Clean energy source success Democrat very much misunderstood at first

parts.note: a win is a success
D is the abbreviation for Democrat
far means very much, as in far better

indicators.note: what comes at first is the opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: first letter of misunderstood

explanation.surface: A green energy policy that succeeded but which a Democrat politician badly misread at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very much misunderstood' reads as one phrase, but very much is FAR on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A wind farm is a group of turbines generating electricity without burning fuel, a renewable power source.

clue.text: I censor a different summary of play

indicators.note: made different means changed, so the letters take on a changed order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A censor admits cutting a theatre synopsis into a new version.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Different' sits where an adjective for summary would go, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is an outline of the plot of a play or film, giving its scenes.

clue.text: Cut down river crossing, having advanced earlier

indicators.note: having something earlier places it in front, setting the order of the pieces

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for advanced, as in A level
a bridge crosses a river

explanation.surface: Troops destroyed a bridge over a river after pushing forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut down' suggests felling or demolition, but it means shortening a text.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a book is to shorten it by condensing, so it is cut down.

clue.text: Old country record about odd bits of rustic area

indicators.note: turning about means facing the other way, so the letters go backwards

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: the odd bits are those in odd-numbered positions, first, third and fifth

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters of rustic
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: An old rural recording about a quaint corner of the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old country' reads like 'the old country' of rustic nostalgia, but it is the historic name of a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Persia was the former Western name for Iran, officially changed in 1935, so a nation of the past.

clue.text: Nearly sober, lacking any boundaries, you might get this pierced

indicators.note: without boundaries means the edges are gone, so only the inner letters survive

parts.note: nearly without its first and last letters
sober without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone almost sober and uninhibited might go out and get a piercing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly' wants to modify sober, but it is fodder itself, and both words lose their outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft fleshy lower part of the ear is the commonest place for a jewellery piercing.

clue.text: Conservative remains popular, making profit

definitions.note: the answer is a verb phrase, to cash in; the definition is its participle form

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
ash is what remains after burning
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A Tory politician stays well liked while turning a nice profit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remains' looks like a verb, but it is the noun for leftover matter.
explanation.definitionFit: To cash in is to take advantage of something for financial gain, so it is profiting.

clue.text: Lived among fish, crouched in fear

indicators.note: something among others is surrounded by them, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: a cod is a fish
were means existed or lived

explanation.surface: Someone who lived among sharks and other fish, always cringing in terror.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lived' is the past of 'be' in the sense of exist: 'they were' here means they lived.
explanation.definitionFit: To cower is to shrink down or huddle in fright, exactly a frightened crouch.

clue.text: Refers to views on the radio

indicators.note: radio is heard not seen, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: views are sights, which sounds identical

explanation.surface: A broadcaster mentions opinions expressed on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Views' suggests opinions on a talk show, but it means sights, as in scenery.
explanation.definitionFit: To cite is to quote or mention something as evidence, which is to refer to it.

clue.text: Using reason, artificial intelligence takes in senior religious figure

indicators.note: to take in is to absorb, so one piece is swallowed inside another

parts.note: AI is the standard abbreviation
a prior is a senior monk, ranking just below an abbot

explanation.surface: A chatbot reasoning logically to win over a high-ranking cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: A priori is Latin for 'from what comes before': knowledge reached by reasoning rather than observation.
explanation.definitionFit: A priori arguments proceed by deduction from principles rather than experience, so they work by logic.

clue.text: Yellowish-green river leaves boy wanting more

indicators.note: to leave is to depart, so that letter goes out of the word

parts.note: Oliver Twist is the workhouse boy who famously asked for more
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A boy, green with envy, departs the riverbank still hungry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like foliage beside yellowish-green, but it is a verb; Oliver Twist is Dickens's orphan who asks 'Please, sir, I want some more.'
explanation.definitionFit: Olive is the dull yellowish-green colour of unripe olives.

clue.text: Firm made up for losing face

indicators.note: the face is the front, so losing it drops the opening letter

parts.note: to atone is to make up for a wrong

explanation.surface: A company makes amends after a public humiliation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' wants to be a company and 'made up' cosmetics, but firm is the adjective and made up for means compensated.
explanation.definitionFit: Toned muscles are tight and well-defined, so a toned body is solid rather than flabby.

clue.text: Zeus's daughter paid her to, strangely

indicators.note: something done strangely is done oddly, so the letters come out in an unusual order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The king of the gods oddly bribed his own daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: In Homer, Aphrodite is the child of Zeus and Dione, though Hesiod has her rising from the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphrodite, Greek goddess of love, is named in Homer's Iliad as a child of Zeus.

clue.text: Prods mum to fill in second name for representative

indicators.note: filling a space puts something inside it, so these pieces go between others

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
to prod is to poke
ma is mum
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Someone nudges their mother to write a middle name on an official form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second name' reads as surname or middle name, but second and name are separate abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: A spokesman speaks on behalf of a group or organisation, so he represents it.

clue.text: Sheep extremely restless in vessels

parts.note: a ewe is a female sheep

indicators.note: the extremes of something are its two ends, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of restless

explanation.surface: Agitated sheep being transported on ships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessels' suggests boats carrying livestock, but here it means containers for liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large wide-mouthed jug, a kind of container for water.
